subject.title: Feature: Trigger model fallback on context length exceeded

question: Should context overflow ever advance to a larger configured model fallback after compaction and oversized-tool-result truncation are exhausted, or should it remain compaction-only?
rationale: Both choices are defensible: larger-context fallback may recover long sessions, but it changes core provider/model routing and can replay unsafe work unless the policy is tightly constrained.

options.title: Implement guarded larger-context fallback
options.body: Allow fallback only after local recovery is exhausted, only to candidates with sufficient effective context headroom, and only when replay/delivery safety checks pass.

options.title: Keep compaction-only overflow policy
options.body: Leave overflow outside model fallback and update docs/error copy so users know to reset, compact, or choose a larger model manually.

options.title: Split diagnostics first
options.body: Land clearer overflow diagnostics and model-switch guidance while deferring automatic fallback policy to a later design decision.

recommendation.title: Implement guarded larger-context fallback
recommendation.body: Allow fallback only after local recovery is exhausted, only to candidates with sufficient effective context headroom, and only when replay/delivery safety checks pass.
